title: What is verification of competency?
description: Verification of competency (VOC) confirms a trained worker can perform a task safely at a specific site. What it involves, who assesses it and an example.
shortAnswer: A verification of competency (VOC) is a documented assessment that confirms a worker who already holds training, a license or experience can perform a specific task safely and correctly, using the equipment, procedures and conditions of a particular workplace. It is common in mining, construction and other high risk industries, and is usually completed before a worker starts the task on site and repeated at set intervals.
keyTakeaways: VOC checks current, site specific ability; it does not replace a license or nationally recognized qualification where one is required.
Australia's Office of the Federal Safety Commissioner, for example, defines VOC as a documented evaluation of a person's skill level against defined competency standards.
A credible VOC uses a documented assessment standard, a competent assessor and a signed record.
A letter from a supervisor saying a worker is competent is not, on its own, accepted as evidence under federal safety accreditation guidance.

sections.heading: What does verification of competency involve?

blocks.text: Verification of competency involves an assessor observing and questioning a worker against a documented standard for a specific task, then recording the result. The Office of the Federal Safety Commissioner (OFSC) [fact sheet on mobile plant](https://www.fsc.gov.au/sites/default/files/2021-09/Fact%20Sheet%20Verification%20of%20Competency%20-%20Mobile%20Plant.pdf) quotes its Evidence Guide definition: "a method of documented evaluation of the skill level of a person against defined competency standards in order to evaluate the person's ability to carry out the relevant activity or works."

The same fact sheet says a formal VOC should be completed or confirmed by the accredited company to an acceptable level, include a detailed and documented assessment standard, be completed by a person who meets minimum competency as an assessor for the item of plant, and be evidenced by a signed, completed VOC assessment.

sections.heading: Where is verification of competency used?

blocks.text: VOC is used mainly in industries where the consequences of error are severe: mining and quarrying, construction, energy, transport and heavy industry. In Australia, for example, the [NSW Resources Regulator](https://www.resources.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-05/operating-mobile-plant-verification-of-competency.pdf) describes VOC as "a method of assessment that can be used to demonstrate workers ability to operate equipment and/or undertake the responsibilities of their role" and connects it to the duty to provide information, training and instruction under clause 39 of the NSW Work Health and Safety Regulation 2017, and to training duties and records under the Work Health and Safety (Mines and Petroleum Sites) Regulation 2022.

The NSW regulator's material points assessors to units of competency on training.gov.au, using their elements, performance criteria, performance evidence and knowledge evidence as a basis for site VOC checklists. Under Australian Government building work accreditation, Office of the Federal Safety Commissioner (OFSC) audit criterion H16.8 requires a system that defines competency requirements for operating mobile plant, which may combine licenses, RTO training and a VOC process.

sections.heading: How is verification of competency different from a competency assessment or a license?

blocks.text: A license or nationally recognized qualification shows a person was assessed as competent at some point; a VOC shows they can do the task here and now, on this equipment, under these procedures. VOC is a type of [competency assessment](/glossary/competency-assessment), usually shorter and narrower than the assessment for a full unit of competency.

blocks.text: Tracking VOC results against every role and task is typically done in a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix). The contrast between recording attendance and verifying ability is explained in [completion tracking vs competency verification](/compare/completion-tracking-vs-competency-verification).

sections.heading: What does a verification of competency record contain?

blocks.text: Illustrative example: a quarry verifies a newly hired wheel loader operator who holds a statement of attainment from a previous employer.

items: **Standard:** the site VOC checklist, based on the relevant unit of competency and the site traffic management plan.
**Practical:** prestart check, loading to the site's haul trucks, parking and isolation, observed by an assessor who is both a qualified assessor and a competent loader operator.
**Knowledge:** questions on site traffic rules, emergency procedures and exclusion zones.
**Record:** checklist, answers, assessor details, date, equipment model and a signed outcome.
**Follow up:** the operator is verified for this loader model only; a reverification date is set in the training matrix.

blocks.text: Setting up a VOC system is covered in [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry supports hybrid verification: digital knowledge checks generated from the framework, paired with structured practical observation records. Both are linked to the same competency and its source procedure, so a change to the procedure flags the verifications that depend on it.

faqs.a: No. A VOC is an employer or site process, not a nationally recognized credential. It does not result in a statement of attainment. Where a regulation requires a license or a specific qualification, a VOC cannot substitute for it; it adds site specific assurance on top.

It depends on the site's system, but federal safety guidance expects someone who is competent as an assessor and also competent in the item of plant, or a team that collectively meets both requirements. An assessment by someone without those competencies, or a supervisor's letter alone, is weak evidence.

faqs.q: How often should VOC be repeated?
faqs.a: There is no single national interval. Sites set reverification periods based on risk, and trigger a new VOC when equipment, procedures or site conditions change, after an incident, or after a long period away from the task. The interval and triggers should be written into the site's safety management system.

faqs.q: Can a VOC be done with an online quiz?
faqs.a: An online quiz can cover the knowledge part, but VOC is fundamentally about observed performance. Guidance from both the NSW Resources Regulator and the OFSC describes practical, documented assessment against a defined standard, which requires observing the person do the task.
